about: Record of the independent check of the benchmark and of every proof file in this folder. The benchmark (question sets, scoring program, ingestion profiler) was built by NEO. These checks were performed with Claude Code, Anthropic's AI coding agent, using Claude Opus 5.5, on 2026-11-04. The OpenHands checks (openhands_reports), the refreshed code_checks and the database re-run on the final code (database_contents) were added on 2026-11-10; OpenHands 600 runs 2 and 3 were added, and the OpenHands Dev 50 reports removed, on 2026-11-12.

terms.question_set: A fixed list of questions about a fixed collection of GitHub issues: 60 for the three sets below, 600 for OpenHands 600.
terms.attempt: One try at answering one question. In the three sets below every question was asked 3 times, so each question has 3 attempts, each marked right or wrong on its own. OpenHands 600 asks each question once per run, and it was run three times.

frozen_files_unchanged.detail: The SymPy issue file and the frozen SymPy Core 50 question file match the SHA-256 fingerprints recorded when they were frozen (verification_bench/SPLITS.sha256). The question file the runs used has the same 50 questions and the same expected answers as the frozen original; only internal category labels differ.

expected_answers_rederived.detail: Every expected answer for a one-answer question was worked out again from the raw issue data by a separate program that shares no code with the benchmark.
expected_answers_rederived.self_test: 3 deliberately wrong expected answers planted in a copy were all detected.

reports_use_these_questions.detail: All 12 stored question reports contain exactly the questions and expected answers in the question files, use gpt-4o for answering and judging, are marked valid, and pass their built-in sanity questions. Every report asks each question 3 times, except the single-attempt confirmation run (foreman-fresh-v8).

stored_verdicts_reproduced.detail: Every one-answer attempt in every stored report was marked again with the benchmark's scoring program. All verdicts match, except 7 in the raw original report (foreman-fresh-baseline/report.json), which are exactly the 7 correct answers the earlier scoring rules wrongly rejected; its corrected copy (report.regraded.json) matches 132 of 132.

scores_recomputed.detail: Every headline score in every stored report equals the score recomputed from its individual attempts.

failed_attempts_read.detail: Every failed attempt in the re-run reports was read. All 11 failed one-answer attempts of the original version are genuinely wrong (for example '44 issues tagged bug' when the answer is 4, or 'no users commented' when four did).
failed_attempts_read.summaries_note: Summaries are marked by an AI judge and are less certain. On issue #1830 (Hugging Face 50) the original's two failed summaries read much like its passing one, so those two failures are probably judge noise. On issue #15623 the original's failed summaries miss the actual LaTeX error, so failing them is fair; the branch's one failed summary there is borderline.

reports_match_the_code.detail: Each report records a fingerprint of the code it tested. Recomputing those fingerprints from the code ties every report to the version it claims. foreman-fresh-v6 was run on an uncommitted copy and cannot be tied to a commit; nothing in OPTIMISATION.md relies on it.

foreman-fresh-v7/report.json.tested_code: an earlier commit (14166da) from before the branch history was tidied; that commit is not in this branch

foreman-fresh-v8/report.json.tested_code: the code of commit 258000c (fingerprint dfabe9557c84d2ce); it was run on 29f7c1b, an earlier commit with the same code from before the history was tidied, which is not in this branch

rerun/branch-neutral-example-sympy2-dev..tested_code: the branch with the group E tidy-ups made by 3 November (fingerprint 4e92f26a44597e9a). It differs from the final code only in the reaction fix, the eval suite's judge option and comments; the assistant does not use the judge option

query_checker_on_original_failures.detail: The query checker was run over the queries behind the original version's failed one-answer attempts in the re-run. It warns on 8 of 11: all 5 two-step questions, plus the comment-count, people-who-opened-issues and top-author questions. The 3 it does not flag are the 'tagged bug' capitalisation mistake, which the instruction changes address.

database_contents.detail: Identical database contents to the original at 5, 20 and 60 issues and with richer model output, and behaviour changes 1 to 4 of OPTIMISATION.md section 6 reproduced (item 7 is covered by test/integration/cypher.test.ts). See profile/repeat-runs.json, database_comparison. On 2026-11-10 the 5, 20 and 60 issue runs were repeated on the final code, after the reaction fix: every item and every link matched the original's (22 items and 16 links, 109 and 95, 388 and 357), with 51, 212 and 620 requests on the original against 41, 89 and 209 on the branch.

code_checks.detail: On the final branch code: type check passes; 620 of 620 unit tests pass (37 files) and 13 of 13 integration tests pass against a real Neo4j; style check reports 26 problems in the whole project against 29 before the changes, none introduced by this branch; the benchmark's own scoring and data-integrity self-tests all pass.

openhands_reports.detail: The six OpenHands 600 reports (qa/rerun/baseline-oh-600-run{1,2,3}.json and branch-oh-600-run{1,2,3}.json) each contain exactly the 150 questions and expected answers of the pinned question file, are marked valid, and pass their sanity questions. Each was re-graded with the corrected grader and every verdict stayed the same. Every stored score equals the score recomputed from its attempts. Code fingerprints: original 98bff512a1c301a8 = commit 3cd3dde in all three runs; branch 6883fbc3d64d73bb = commit 10d6ea3 in run 1, and 97ffa01b9e7fc8a9 = commit 5ad56c6 in runs 2 and 3.
openhands_reports.note: These runs used gpt-4o-2024-08-06 to answer and claude-haiku-5.5 to judge the summaries, all through OpenRouter, unlike the 12 reports above, which used gpt-4o for both. The original's 'comment_reactions_match' check fails in all three baseline reports (section 6, item 7 of OPTIMISATION.md).
